collection.description: I promise. The spring, when they get there, is tiny, clear and bubbling, in a nest of roots under a fig tree.

ask.text:
(child) has found a spring in the jungle that no grown-up knows about. (child.He/She) says the water tastes like sugarcane, and that anyone who drinks from it feels like running all day. (child.He/She) has told no one else, except now (child.he/she) has told (subject), because (subject) is (subject.his/her) favourite grown-up and has a bad back.
"Come and see," (child) says, pulling at (subject)'s hand. "It'll fix your back. I promise." The spring, when they get there, is tiny, clear and bubbling, in a nest of roots under a fig tree. A ring of very small footprints goes all the way round it.
Should (subject) drink from the children's spring?

c1o1.text: (subject) stands up, and (subject.his/her) back doesn't hurt. Then (subject.he/she) realises (subject.his/her) hair is falling over (subject.his/her) eyes, thick and luscious, and (subject.his/her) hands are smooth. (child) is jumping up and down. "I TOLD you." It turns out the children have all been drinking from it, which explains a great deal about how much energy they have. (subject) runs home. (subject) has not run anywhere in years.

c1o2.text: (subject) is very thirsty. (subject.He/She) drinks and drinks. (child) tugs at (subject.his/her) sleeve, saying, "That's enough, that's enough," and (subject) doesn't stop until (subject.he/she) looks up and finds (subject.he/she) is only a head taller than (child). (subject) is fifteen. (child) looks at (subject.him/her) with deep disappointment. "You're not a grown-up now," (child.he/she) says. "You're just BIG."

c1.text: (subject) kneels, which hurts, and drinks from (subject.his/her) cupped hands. The water is sweet, and fizzy, and makes (subject.his/her) teeth tingle. (child) watches (subject.him/her) very hard, waiting...

c2o1.text: The tingle goes all over (subject.his/her) face and stops at (subject.his/her) neck. When (subject) looks in the spring, a young face looks back, bright and smooth, with not a line on it. The rest of (subject.him/her), (subject.his/her) back included, is exactly the same. (child) is annoyed. "That's not how you do it," (child.he/she) says. "You're meant to drink it."

c2o2.text: Nothing happens, except that (subject.his/her) face feels very clean. (subject) and (child) sit by the spring for an hour, and (child) tells (subject.him/her) all the other secrets the children have that no grown-up knows about. Some of them are alarming. (subject) promises not to tell anyone, and doesn't, though (subject.he/she) does go and check that the old well has a cover on it.

c2.text: (subject) doesn't trust water that makes children run all day. (subject.He/She) cups a little and splashes it on (subject.his/her) face, then sits back on (subject.his/her) heels and lets it drip...
